mechanisms.sameOriginBrowser: A browser request may cross the service boundary only from the exact local product origin. This is a CSRF boundary, not remote machine identity.
mechanisms.operatorCredential: A valid Agent X operator token admits remote administrative access at the service boundary; route-local requirements may still apply.
mechanisms.scopedMachineCredential: A purpose-specific credential is admitted only to its declared route family and, for complete enforcement, is validated again by the route-owned contract.
mechanisms.typedConfirmation: An irreversible delete, bulk replacement, or restore requires an exact non-boolean phrase bound to the action or selected resource. Reversible stop, cancel, lease-release, and ephemeral maintenance controls are tracked in separate consequence tiers.
mechanisms.routeLocalValidator: Authorization logic owned by the route or its mounted router runs after the global boundary. Ordinary payload/schema validation is not counted here.

limitations: The global Core, Benchmark, and RAG boundaries intentionally admit headerless loopback callers and, when explicitly enabled, product-internal service hosts. That local topology admission is not a scoped machine credential.
Static evidence proves checked-in middleware placement and exact route coverage; it does not replace wrong-host, wrong-token, cross-site, or browser journey tests.
CI rejects missing or stale route audits and reports any enforcementStatus=gap entry explicitly; the current checked-in matrix has no unresolved authorization gap.
The matrix evaluates declared route actions. Conditional behavior inside one route may still need finer action-variant authorization in a future schema.

core.limitation: publicExposureGuard admits operator tokens, exact local same-origin UI, headerless loopback, and explicitly enabled product-internal hosts; scoped tokens are path-limited but do not replace route-local validation.

benchmark.limitation: createApiHostGuard protects every /api mutation while retaining loopback and explicitly enabled product-internal machine calls. Benchmark defines no route-scoped machine credential in this inventory.

rag.limitation: createApiHostGuard protects every /api mutation while retaining loopback and explicitly enabled product-internal machine calls. Snapshot routes additionally require the recovery token.

action-observation.note: The service boundary is the authorization contract for this non-safe observation action.

user-mutation.note: The service boundary is the authorization contract for this non-destructive user mutation unless an exact override records a stronger route gate.

destructive-mutation.note: The destructive route is globally admitted but has no verified exact typed-confirmation phrase.

scoped-machine-call.note: The machine action currently relies on the global local/operator boundary and has no verified purpose-scoped credential plus route-local validator.

irreversible-delete-bulk-or-restore.description: Deletes durable product data or artifacts, replaces persisted configuration/state, performs a restore, or executes a bulk archival/removal operation. Exact typed confirmation is required.

reversible-runtime-control.description: Stops or cancels active work, releases a lease, resets a reversible routing state, or performs bounded runtime recovery. Typed confirmation would add friction without protecting durable data; an observable acknowledgement/recovery path remains required.

ephemeral-maintenance.description: Clears rebuildable in-process cache state without deleting durable product records. Typed confirmation is not required.
